_doc: The shared drives WP-H1 ingests, and the visibility everything derived from
Starting set, chosen 2026-08-28: the three drives every employee can already
IDs enumerated 2026-08-30 via drives.list under domain-wide delegation. Matching
by NAME would have been ambiguous and this is the evidence: the tenant has ten
shared drives and three of them begin with "BizDev" — BizDev, BizDev DataHub and
"BizDev <-> Ops". An ID is what the API takes and the only thing a rename does
read. That is deliberate as a first cut — a drive whose membership is the
whole company cannot leak to the whole company, so the isolation tests can
come before the drives that need them rather than after.
drive.readonly scope we already need, so the connector reads the IDs itself
and records them here. Names are for people; IDs are what the API takes and
the only thing stable across a rename.
Adding a drive with narrower membership means adding it with the visibility
its membership implies — NOT internal. ADR-0013 makes every derived artefact
inherit the strictest classification of its sources, so getting this wrong
here is how a client-confidential document ends up quoted in a summary that

drives.name: All
drives.why: readable by everyone in the company

drives.name: BizDev
drives.why: readable by everyone in the company

drives.name: Delivery
drives.why: readable by everyone in the company
